clue.text: Most of expected share for the time being

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept here

parts.note: something expected is due
a ration is a person's allotted share

explanation.surface: Someone is told they will get most of the portion they expected, at least for now.
explanation.definitionFit: A duration is the period something lasts, as in the phrase for the duration, meaning for as long as the present lasts.

clue.text: I'd help to reinterpret classical site

indicators.note: reinterpreting the words means reading their letters in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scholar offers to help explain an ancient site.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was the ancient Greek sanctuary of the oracle of Apollo, a famous classical site.

clue.text: Note son steeped in additional regret

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: steeped in means placed right inside a piece

parts.note: additional means more

explanation.surface: A note says a son is consumed by extra regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong done, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Crooked dealer gives card to solicitor

parts.note: a ticket can be a printed card giving entry
a tout is one who solicits custom, not a lawyer here

explanation.surface: A crooked dealer passes a card to his lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer; here it is simply one who solicits. A TICKET TOUT sells tickets on at inflated prices, often outside venues.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket tout resells event tickets at a profit, a shady trader or dealer.

clue.text: Perhaps tipped porter when starting journey home

definitions.text: Perhaps tipped porter when starting journey home

parts.words: Perhaps tipped porter when starting journey home
parts.note: porter suggests a railway porter given a tip, but it is dark beer, tipped down the throat as a final drink before leaving

explanation.surface: A traveller hands a railway porter a tip at the start of the trip home.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter is a dark British beer, and tipped means poured down the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a last alcoholic drink taken before setting off home.

clue.text: Reptile found in part of Cornish coast

definitions.meaning: the peninsula at the southern tip of Cornwall, a county in the far south-west of England

explanation.surface: A naturalist spots a reptile somewhere along the Cornish coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile is the common creature, and the Lizard peninsula is the most southerly point of mainland Britain.

clue.text: One to the fore, in Russian history

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the van, short for vanguard, is the front position

explanation.surface: Someone comes to prominence in Russia's past.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible and other tsars of that name are major figures from Russia's past.

clue.text: Suffer number about to turn up, in a flap

parts.note: to ail is to suffer illness

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a figure will appear, leaving them in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' turns NO and RE together into ERON. 'in a flap' suggests panic, but it is a wing part.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged control surface on an aircraft wing, a kind of flap.

clue.text: On the surface, they go along with wild shindig European held

definitions.text: On the surface, they go along

indicators.note: held means the jumbled letters keep the next piece inside them
wild means the letters run riot into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: At a riotous party a European is detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns SHINDIG into DINGHIS; 'held' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Small boats travel along on the surface of the water.

clue.text: Almost feeble hit

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a feeble excuse is a lame one

explanation.surface: A punch that was very nearly too weak to count.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is an informal verb meaning to thrash or strike hard.

clue.text: Dejected, as waves are seen breaking?

definitions.meaning: when a wave breaks its top, the crest, falls

explanation.surface: Someone watching the surf feels gloomy as the breakers come in.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into CREST FALLEN: the crest of a breaking wave tumbles down.
explanation.definitionFit: Crestfallen describes someone whose spirits have dropped after a disappointment, a synonym for downcast.

clue.text: Parking illegally? That's fine by me!

definitions.text: Parking illegally? That's fine by me!

parts.words: Parking illegally? That's fine by me!
parts.note: sounds like someone shrugging off bad parking, but fine is a penalty this official happily issues

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully says they do not mind cars being left where they should not be.
explanation.walkthrough: A British traffic warden patrols streets and tickets parking offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: This official imposes penalties on drivers who leave vehicles in the wrong place.

clue.text: In the event, she gets up in time to take part

definitions.text: In the event, she gets up in time to take part

parts.words: In the event, she gets up in time to take part
parts.note: reads like a late riser, but the event is a show-jumping or eventing competition and getting up means mounting her mount

explanation.surface: In the end, a woman manages to get out of bed in time to join in.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rider in an equestrian event climbs into the saddle before competing.

clue.text: This bend requires some gear-changing

indicators.note: some of the words gives a run of their letters, sitting across the hyphen

explanation.surface: A driver warns that a particular corner demands a lot of gear changes.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved structure, so it is a bend or bow shape.

clue.text: Writing as a doctor, he 'offered report of homes with many storeys

definitions.text: Writing as a doctor, he 'offered report of homes with many storeys

parts.words: Writing as a doctor, he 'offered report of homes with many storeys
parts.note: homes sounds like Holmes and storeys like stories: an author narrating as Dr Watson told many Sherlock Holmes stories

explanation.surface: A doctor offers an account of tall residential buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: The author narrated through Dr Watson; 'homes' suggests houses but is said like Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator of Sherlock Holmes, a doctor himself, wrote the stories through his narrator Dr Watson.

clue.text: Go to try out drum kit?

definitions.meaning: go away, as an order to leave
a drummer testing a kit would strike it

explanation.surface: A drummer is invited to have a go on a new set of drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a slang command to clear off, and to beat a drum is to strike it.

clue.text: Move in a pet cat, put on floor

indicators.note: in an across answer the cat is placed after the floor letters

parts.note: an ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: An owner moves their pet cat and sets it down on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a pet is an old phrase for in a sulk or huff.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce is to stalk off in an exaggerated huff, which is moving in a pet.

clue.text: One that's learned what's not relevant

definitions.meaning: of theoretical interest only, with no practical bearing

explanation.surface: A scholar's knowledge is beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a university scholar and a point that is merely theoretical.

clue.text: Party in vehicle going alongside river

indicators.note: the river is placed next to the vehicle, after it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A party travels by car beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry noisily, which is to party.

clue.text: No way to get in fruity retort

indicators.note: getting in means going inside another piece

parts.note: fruity suggests ripe, like mature fruit
O, a zero, means no or nothing
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A rude reply blocks the way into something saucy.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick sharp reply, which is a retort.

clue.text: Yellow bird about at first

indicators.note: the letter for about comes at the front, before the bird

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: A yellow bird is fluttering about near the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven also means cowardly.

clue.text: Empty pipe?

definitions.meaning: to drain or use up completely
the tailpipe carrying fumes from an engine

explanation.surface: A pipe with nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to empty completely and is also the pipe expelling engine fumes.

clue.text: Whatever's happened, it's in a mess

explanation.surface: Whatever has gone on, things are chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in any case and also in a careless, disorderly way.

clue.text: Fool needing to be paid to admit parking?

indicators.note: to admit means to let something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bill needing to be paid is due
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A fool is told they must pay up for using a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to fool or trick them.

clue.text: Occasionally two-timing?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, two times: one present moment and one past moment

explanation.surface: Someone is only sometimes unfaithful to a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at irregular intervals, and it names two times, the present and a past moment.

clue.text: It works like a charm, with two incomplete projects

indicators.note: two means the piece is used twice
incomplete means the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out

explanation.surface: Two half-done projects nevertheless work perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts JUTS to JU, and 'two' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A juju is a West African fetish or amulet believed to have magical power, a kind of charm.

clue.text: Girl heard guy lied badly about daughter, following wrong advice

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
badly means the letters are put together in a poor, jumbled way

explanation.surface: A girl hears that a man lied clumsily about her daughter, and acts on bad advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl heard' looks like a girl overhearing; it is the title Miss said aloud. 'badly' scrambles the man's words into GUIEDLY, and 'about' wraps that round the daughter's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting misguidedly means acting under mistaken guidance, as when following bad advice.

clue.text: Sound disgusted

parts.note: both an instruction to sound revolted and the noise a revolted person makes

explanation.surface: Someone is told to sound revolted.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection is the grunt people make to express disgust or horror.

clue.text: Vet heard giving order to pay

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to vet something is to check it

explanation.surface: A vet is overheard giving instructions about a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank draft written by an account holder is a written order to a bank to pay money.

clue.text: Submarine movement gave town rude shock

indicators.note: a shock of hair is tousled, so these letters are tangled up

explanation.surface: A town is rudely jolted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' rearranges TOWN RUDE; 'Submarine' here means simply beneath the sea, not a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a current flowing beneath the surface of the sea, an underwater movement.
